text.p: German steel and engineering group Thyssen AG said on Friday it would reorganize its industrial portfolio into five primary and an equal number of secondary profit centres.

After announcing it would cut its dividend payout to eight marks from 10 as profit in the business year to September 30 plunged to 350 million marks from 775 million, it said the following activities would make up its core business:
As secondary profit centres with the potential of beoming core business, the company named:
It was not immediately clear whether the restructuring of the portfolio would affect the corporate structure of the company.
Thyssen is currently organised into a holding company, Thyssen AG, with three operative industrial divisions: Thyssen Stahl AG, Thyssen Industrie AG and Thyssen Handel AG.
The company's car components division, Budd Co of the United States, has operated directly under the supervision of the holding company.

Thyssen said in a regulatory statement that the restructuring measures were fully reflected in its 1995/96 balance sheet and that the company would divest loss-making and non-core activities that were not of strategic importance.
"This process is underway," the company said.
